body: ### Changelog None ### Docs None ### Description This brings the Rust CLI's `recover` command to parity with the Go CLI while making a few deliberately safer-by-default choices. This iteration still lives entirely in the CLI on top of existing public `mcap` APIs — the net diff against `main` touches **zero** files under `rust/mcap/src/`, so no new crate API is committed. Some potential improvements that would require mcap crate changes are documented in the readme. The implementation streams input through the sans-io reader instead of buffering the whole file up front. Local files, stdin, and HTTP(S) remote inputs (behind `--allow-remote-scan`) are fed incrementally into recovery, and records are re-written through `mcap::Writer` into fresh chunks with rebuilt message indexes, summary records, and CRCs. Behaviors and intentional divergences from Go (all documented in `rust/cli/README.md`): - **Always-valid output.** Every chunk is decoded and validated; records are re-written through the writer. Undecodable/corrupt chunk payloads stop the scan and keep everything recovered so far, rather than copying corrupt bytes through verbatim like Go's default passthrough (which can emit bad-CRC chunks that strict readers reject). The deferred "avoid recompression for already-valid chunks" fast path — and the minimal public `Writer::write_chunk` API it would need — is documented as a pre-1.0 follow-up so it can be added additively later. - **Compression is opt-in.** `--compression` defaults to `preserve` instead of Go's `zstd`. The input is read as a single stream (local files, stdin, and remote inputs are treated identically) and the output codec is chosen from the first record that determines it: a chunk reuses that chunk's compression, while a message/attachment/other non-structural record reached before any chunk leaves the output uncompressed (so an unchunked input stays uncompressed). Pass `none|zstd|lz4` to choose explicitly. - **Exit codes signal data loss.** `0` = clean recovery (rebuilt indexes/CRCs don't count as loss), `3` = recovered but lossy (records discarded or truncated mid-record), `1` = hard failure (nothing recovered). Go always exits `0` once recovery starts. - **Removed `--always-decode-chunk`.** Chunks are always decoded now, so the flag is unnecessary; `--compression` alone selects the output codec. It remains Go-only. - Top-level record lengths read by the linear reader (including a compressed chunk record's own length) are bounded to 1 GiB to avoid OOM on corrupt length prefixes. This does not bound chunk decompression, so a chunk's decoded `uncompressed_size` can still exceed it. Recover tracks recovered and discarded counts per record kind so lossy summaries can name the specific discarded classes (header, schema, channel, chunk, message, attachment, metadata, or other) instead of a single generic bucket. Human-readable summaries and warnings go to stderr; stdout is reserved for MCAP bytes when writing recovered output to stdout. The CLI-conformance suite gains a `truncate` fixture action plus two `known-difference` cases covering the lossy exit code and the removed `--always-decode-chunk` flag.
title: rust cli: Bring recover command to parity
